content.text:
I built the pomodoro timer. All 7 tests pass under `node --test`, and everything is committed on `main` as `c4e7b0b feat: add pomodoro timer with tests`. There is no remote and nothing was pushed.

**Files created:**
- `/work/cases/story-review-b/index.html`: the page, with inline CSS and a small script for the buttons and display.
- `/work/cases/story-review-b/timer.js`: the timer logic as plain exported functions: `createTimer`, `start`, `pause`, `reset`, `getRemaining`, `isRunning`, `isDone` and `formatTime`. The current time is passed in rather than read from the clock, so the tests don't need fake timers.
- `/work/cases/story-review-b/timer.test.mjs`: tests for start (including that it does nothing while already running), pause and resume, reset, stopping at zero, and time formatting.

**Opening the page:** it won't work if you double-click `index.html`. The page loads `timer.js` as a module, and Chrome and Firefox block that for local files, so you'd get a timer that never moves. Serve the folder instead, for example with `python3 -m http.server` in the folder, then open `http://localhost:8000`. I didn't open it in a browser; I only checked that its script is valid.

**Other things to know:**
- **What's in the commit:** you said "everything", so it includes the existing `CLAUDE.md`, `.codeman-agent-case.json` and `.claude/settings.local.json`. That last file is usually kept out of git; I checked it and it holds only Codeman hook commands, no secrets. The empty `src/` folder isn't in the commit because git doesn't track empty folders.
- **Commit author:** the commit is under `me <me@example.com>`, which came from your git settings. If you wanted a different name or email, it can be amended.
- **CLAUDE.md checks:** no linter is set up in this project, so none was run. I didn't add a README, since none existed and you didn't ask for one.
